findings.title: Create a fresh queue pool for each partition assignment
findings.body: The factory creates its queue pool only once and passes that same pool to every strategy. Closing or joining a strategy shuts down that pool's workers and queues, but a Kafka rebalance subsequently calls create_with_partitions on the same factory and receives another strategy backed by the stopped pool. New messages then either accumulate without workers or fail to enqueue and are marked completed by submit's exception handler, allowing unprocessed results to be committed. Allocate assignment-scoped workers and offset tracking when creating each strategy.

findings.title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
findings.body: Each work queue is created with no maximum size, and submit always accepts more messages without raising MessageRejected. If processing is slower than Kafka ingestion, or a worker stalls, the consumer continues retaining decoded results and original messages indefinitely. The offset tracker also retains all later offsets behind unfinished work. This can exhaust consumer memory under exactly the slow-item workload this mode is intended to handle; queued and in-flight work need a bound with backpressure.

findings.title: Drain accepted work before stopping workers and committing final offsets
findings.body: Graceful shutdown sets every worker's shutdown flag before shutting down the queues. Workers therefore exit after their current item instead of draining queued items, despite shutdown(immediate=False). In addition, strategy.close stops the commit thread before waiting for workers, so results completed during shutdown never receive a final commit. Normal shutdown or partition revocation abandons accepted work and replays already processed results on the next assignment. close/join should drain accepted work (within the supplied timeout) and commit its completed offsets before stopping.

findings.title: Track delivered offset order rather than requiring consecutive Kafka offsets
findings.body: The tracker stops at any integer offset absent from all_offsets, even if every delivered message has completed. Kafka can legitimately deliver nonconsecutive offsets, for example when transactional control records or aborted transactions are skipped. If completed offsets 100 and 102 are present in the same commit scan, it commits only 100 even though 102 is safe; with ongoing work after such gaps this unnecessarily retains completed offsets and increases replay and memory usage. Determine the safe prefix of delivered offsets, stopping at outstanding work rather than at offsets Kafka never delivered.
